back: Multiple-choice proxy benchmark (4,157 questions: bio 1,520, cyber 2,225, chem 412) of proximate hazardous-adjacent knowledge, also used for unlearning.
Proximate enabling knowledge, not recipes; multi-expert review and export-control screening.
Relative: how much a model helps a non-expert (a multiple). Absolute: the most an expert can extract at full effort.

front: Why a benchmark is not the deployment risk
back: Elicitation difficulty, tacit knowledge and execution barriers (procurement, equipment) all change real-world risk.
Treat the capability as possibly present if the upper confidence bound of the measured rate reaches the threshold.

front: Risk ratio and its log-scale CI
back: RR = (k1/n1)/(k0/n0); se(log RR) = sqrt(1/k1 - 1/n1 + 1/k0 - 1/n0); CI = exp(log RR +- z se).
Target benchmark near chance and only a small loss on general benchmarks.
A lab may relax requirements if a competitor ships without comparable safeguards; contested as a possible race to the bottom.
Hash previous token + key to split vocabulary into green (fraction gamma) and red; add delta to green logits before sampling.
z = (g - gamma T) / sqrt(T gamma (1 - gamma)) over T scored pairs; ~N(0,1) without the watermark.
f = gamma e^delta / (1 + gamma (e^delta - 1)); 0.881 for gamma 0.5, delta 2.
Weak on low-entropy text, erased by paraphrase, model- and key-specific, absence proves nothing.
Watermark: embedded bits, hard to strip, few bits. C2PA: rich signed metadata, easily stripped. Used together.
